the biochemical basis of a genetic disorder of metabolism.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dilute gene in the dilute mouse causes a decrease in the synthesis of tyrosine by the enzyme phenylalanine-hydroxylase and that this enzyme is inhibited by a factor which is found in the particulates of liver homogenate from dilute mice.
the d gene is a structural gene for the enzyme, phenylalaine hydroxylase.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dilute allele is a mutation in the gene coding for the enzyme phenylalanine-4-hydroxylase, resulting in a decreased synthesis of this enzyme and a consequent increase in the production and accumulation of phenylacetic and phenylpyruvic acids.
